comment: Seccomp profile for dai/keycloak:v2.1 (base: quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.6.4-0, ubi9-micro / RHEL 9.8). Allows all Docker-default syscalls and additionally blocks a general-purpose hardening baseline (mount, kernel module loading, kexec, cross-process memory introspection, BPF/perf, swap/hostname, obsolete syscalls). NOTE: the 48 OS-layer CVEs covered by sast/report/keycloak_v2_vulner_report.md (glibc DNS/TSIG/scanf/ungetwc parsing bugs, embedded libpng/harfbuzz/lcms2/zlib bugs inside java-21-openjdk-headless, libgcc demangle stack exhaustion, ncurses, nspr/nss, pcre2, sed TOCTOU, sqlite-libs, zlib) are all application/library-internal logic bugs (out-of-bounds read/write, use-after-free, infinite loop, stack exhaustion) triggered through normal C function calls or JVM-internal native calls -- none of them are identifiable or filterable at the raw syscall granularity. Seccomp therefore CANNOT provide CVE-specific containment here; the CVE-specific containment lives in docker-compose_vm5_secure.yml (cap_drop ALL, read_only root filesystem with named volume/tmpfs for the only writable paths, no-new-privileges). No AppArmor/SELinux custom policy is used (RHEL 9 production runs under Docker's default SELinux container_t confinement with no custom type authored). This profile is general defense-in-depth attack-surface reduction only, consistent with the same rationale documented in seccomp-dagster.json.

syscalls.comment: Block mount-related syscalls. Keycloak (Quarkus/JVM) never mounts filesystems at runtime.
Block kernel module loading (container should never load kernel modules)

Block cross-process memory access / ptrace. JVM/Quarkus does not need to introspect other processes' memory at runtime; also closes off a common post-exploitation primitive for an attacker who reached one of the embedded libpng/harfbuzz/lcms2 native code paths via the java-21-openjdk-headless CVEs.
Block BPF and perf events (privilege escalation / info leakage primitives, not used by Keycloak/Quarkus)
Block swap and hostname changes (not needed by Keycloak)
Block obsolete/legacy syscalls not needed by Keycloak (oprofile dcookie lookup, legacy NFS server control, x86 vm86 mode). General attack-surface reduction.
